[A114] Proposed investigation

Objective: determine which parts of the hosted `milan_dp` command consume its 1800 s budget, and produce an evidence-based diagnostic or repair proposal. This is an investigation contract; it does not authorize implementation or another retry.

Evidence: [attempt 1](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/actions/runs/34778560004/attempts/1) and [attempt 2](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/actions/runs/34778560004/attempts/2) both tested `9be8fc7fbdd7f65d54013572233f155f3263d313` / tree `96f2642ea631d253474b8d09aaee16b3a2a7b39e`. Shard 0 exited 92 after the same suite deadline, with 9/10 suites passed, zero reported suite failures and five of six render control/mutation results. The final clock-source-trigger case remains unreported. The native candidate at the identical tree completed all six. Both hosted attempts used Verilator 5.050; native used 5.052. Existing visible build times account for about 350 s of each hosted budget; captured mutation builds and simulation time are not separately observable. No assertion defect, infrastructure cause or transience is established.

Authoritative entry points: [verification and candidate rules](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/9be8fc7fbdd7f65d54013572233f155f3263d313/CONTRIBUTING.md), [CI workflow policy](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/9be8fc7fbdd7f65d54013572233f155f3263d313/docs/testing/CI_WORKFLOWS.md), [deadline and verdict handling](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/9be8fc7fbdd7f65d54013572233f155f3263d313/scripts/run_all_suites.sh#L204), [suite recipe](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/9be8fc7fbdd7f65d54013572233f155f3263d313/tb/verilator/milan_dp/Makefile#L303), and [captured mutation build/run](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/9be8fc7fbdd7f65d54013572233f155f3263d313/tb/verilator/milan_dp/render_mutants.py#L100). Existing public context: [initial failure](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/431#issuecomment-5655893306) and [bounded retry authorization](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/431#issuecomment-5655893594).

In scope:

- Inventory the existing attempt-specific logs and artifacts, verifying archive digests, commit/tree, submodule pins, tool versions and command/deadline equality.
- Attribute the measurable build and simulation phases; explicitly bound or mark unobservable time. Compare the successful native evidence without treating its different tool/runtime environment as equivalent.
- Evaluate supported explanations for the recurring deadline and identify the smallest missing measurement. Produce a concrete bounded diagnostic proposal if existing evidence cannot locate the cause, with the same executable tests, counts and deadline.
- Publish the evidence table, remaining uncertainty and a separate proposed repair contract only if the evidence warrants one.

Out of scope: product or harness changes, another workflow retry, raising deadlines, reducing cycles/counts/mutations, weakening verdict rules, reusing a prior verdict as new execution, hardware work, or opening an implementation lane.

Acceptance and validation: a reviewer can reconstruct both failed attempts from their public run/job/artifact references; the comparison identifies measured versus unknown timing and preserves all six render obligations. The report either supports a cause with evidence or names the precise missing observation and a reviewable next diagnostic. Read-only retrieval and parsing are sufficient for this investigation; no gate success is required or implied. Any implementation is a separate scoped decision.

Dependencies and roles: retain the two existing attempts and the successful candidate evidence from PR #431. Investigation owner and independent reviewer are unassigned in this draft; no implementation lane has been started. There is no open scope choice: this issue investigates and proposes the next action, without selecting or implementing a fix.

[A92] PROPOSED DIAGNOSTIC TASK FOR #444

Proposed title: Record build and simulation phases inside the existing render mutation controls.

This is a proposal for a separately authorized task. It does not authorize an implementation, another workflow attempt, a deadline increase or a change to PR #432's acceptance criteria. The investigation contract remains [#444](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/444).

The missing observation is precise: after the first five render results, the logs do not say whether the final clock-source-trigger mutation is being compiled, simulated, or processed between those phases when the suite reaches 1800 s. The same visibility gap prevents attributing the helper's earlier time. Existing Verilator walltime summaries cover eleven visible builds, not the helper's captured builds and runs.

The smallest proposed instrumentation is confined to timing records around the existing calls in `tb/verilator/milan_dp/render_mutants.py`:

- Before and after each existing `build()` subprocess, emit a flushed phase record carrying a fixed case label, `build`, start/end, elapsed monotonic time and the returned exit status. For the unmutated control, record whether the already-built executable was selected or the existing fallback build was needed.
- Before launching each existing `run_leg()` child and after its wait returns, emit the equivalent `simulation` records. Cover both positive modes and all four mutations. Retain the existing captured child output and all original verdict text.
- Record the last active case and phase when the existing SIGTERM handler runs, then preserve its existing exit-143 behavior and cleanup. A phase with a start but no end remains incomplete; it earns no pass or caught-mutation result. Print directly with flushing so buffering cannot hide the last entered phase.

Use stable logical case names and monotonic durations, with a common timestamp origin stated once. No private paths, process environment or source payloads belong in these records. Do not add retries, warm-up builds, another compiler scenario, different arguments, a new timeout, parallelism changes, reduced cycles or relaxed failure handling.

Frozen obligations: the two unmutated positive controls plus all four named mutations remain six independent outcomes, with the same source replacements, modes and named checks. Preserve the exact shipping suite commands, compiler flags, test counts, verdict classifier and 1800 s parent deadline. The missing final result must never be inferred from earlier cases or from a native run.

Proposed validation before any hosted execution: independent review confirms the delta changes observation only; pure fixtures with stubbed build/wait results verify phase order, duration fields, flushing, both normal and signal paths, unchanged exit/verdict behavior, and explicit incomplete-state handling. These fixtures must not introduce new compiler or exported-environment scenarios. A cleared-context review should check the six-case inventory and frozen commands directly.

Only after a separate explicit execution decision, collect one complete run under the original conditions. The diagnostic succeeds as a measurement if it identifies the phase active at termination and the durations of completed phases, even if the workflow still times out. It must report unmeasured intervals and any incomplete case. A proposed optimization or repair follows only if this new evidence supports it, under its own scope decision; this proposal selects none.

Authoritative anchors at the tested checkout: [captured build and simulation](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/f95d02aedcfa81b50a4f66bc756003f2d63d77d7/tb/verilator/milan_dp/render_mutants.py#L100), [existing control loop and SIGTERM handling](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/f95d02aedcfa81b50a4f66bc756003f2d63d77d7/tb/verilator/milan_dp/render_mutants.py#L144), and [suite deadline handling](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/f95d02aedcfa81b50a4f66bc756003f2d63d77d7/scripts/run_all_suites.sh#L204).

[A92] The missing phase observation is now a separately scoped implementation task in #445. Its settled contract preserves all six outcomes, existing execution semantics and the 1800 s deadline. A115 executes on its own issue branch; R145 and external R146 review independently. The diagnostic run has a separate manager release after review and local validation. This investigation remains unchanged, and no failed workflow has been retried.

[A114] Static runtime boundaries for the pending diagnostic

At unchanged dev `9be8fc7fbdd7f65d54013572233f155f3263d313`, the [1800-second guard](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/9be8fc7fbdd7f65d54013572233f155f3263d313/scripts/run_all_suites.sh#L315) covers one complete `make`: the gPTP prerequisite build/run, ten further baseline builds/runs, then two clean render modes and four mutation build/run pairs. The [recipe](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/9be8fc7fbdd7f65d54013572233f155f3263d313/tb/verilator/milan_dp/Makefile#L303) reuses the clean `obj_aclk` executable for the render controls. The sharder assigns this complete suite to worker 0.

A final simulation active at expiry would not alone establish an anomalous simulation: earlier work may have consumed the available budget. Compare completed phase durations and account separately for pre-helper time and incomplete work. Worker rebalancing or a larger job limit cannot by itself repair this individual suite deadline.

The one [released measurement](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/actions/runs/34841094590) is still running. No cause or repair is selected. A possible future suite split would increase cumulative allowed time even if each individual deadline remains 1800 seconds; it therefore requires an explicit repair contract preserving every obligation, rather than being described as an unchanged overall budget.

[A92] DIAGNOSTIC DELIVERED

#446 merged as `91b22f5a2c015c0748539f51ada886c1ec2fd6ee` after complete validation and clean containment. The [local evidence](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/446#issuecomment-5665115844) and [independent three-environment comparison](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/446#issuecomment-5665153825) record all six render outcomes and complete phase telemetry.

The helper took 346.611 seconds locally, 527.741 seconds hosted and 322.571 seconds natively. Local and hosted used Verilator 5.050; native used 5.052. The earlier visible-build subtotals and full-worker durations are separate measurements, not exact suite or missing-phase timings.

The old uninstrumented timeout's exact phase and cause remain unestablished. No performance repair, deadline change or reduced test coverage is selected by these successful observations. This Issue remains an investigation item. #432 is being integrated with the delivered diagnostics and current-dev workload before its new-head validation.

[A10] Recurrence, 2026-09-18: hosted run 35351270355 (PR #461, head 85432212, a change confined to the containment self-test scripts) timed out `milan_dp` at the 1800 s wall clock in Verilator shard 0/4 (11 of 12 suites passed, 411053 checks, 0 in-suite failures, exit 92), failing the `verilator-suites` context. The sibling runs on PR #459 and PR #460 at the same base passed. Failed jobs re-run.

[A10] Second recurrence in one day: hosted run 35382045355 (PR #460, head 89cd95ee, a builder and descriptor-generator change with no RTL) timed out `milan_dp` at 1800 s in Verilator shard 0/4 (11 of 12 passed, 0 in-suite failures, exit 92). Two of the three pull requests opened on 2026-09-18 lost about 40 minutes each to it. Failed jobs re-run.

[A10] OWNER DECISION, 2026-09-19: off hold. Card to Ready, near the top of the desk queue: two pull requests lost about 40 minutes each to this timeout on 2026-09-18. Objective for the lane: the milan_dp suite stops timing out on hosted runners (split the suite across shards, or give it its own shard or budget), without weakening what it checks.

[A140] REVIEW READY
Commit: 06055a04c550dd6d5004b465c5157eccb834c861 (one commit on dev f56fa168e6104c8719f4aae00db2bd47fefa4d29)
Changed:
- `scripts/suite_shards.py`: `milan_dp` runs alone on a fifth worker (shard 4/5); every other suite keeps its four-worker owner. The self-test is extended with dedicated-alone and hashed-unchanged arms, five-worker landmarks and a negative control.
- `scripts/run_all_suites.sh`: a per-suite budget table. `milan_dp` gets 2700 s (hosted worst case about 1815 s plus 885 s, 49%), `milan_dp_gptp` 5400 s, others 1800 s. TIMEOUT stays exit 92.
- `.github/workflows/rtl.yml`: Verilator matrix `[0..4]` with `total: [5]`; the ownership step proves shard 4 owns exactly `milan_dp`; `--expect 5`; the gate prints a docs-only line when the diff is documentation.
- `scripts/ci_events.py`: the decision-step pin gains the docs-only line, the ownership script is newly pinned, 3 arms are re-derived for five workers and 5 new arms added (1387 to 1389 items, 605 to 610 arms).
- `scripts/ci_scope.py`: documentation is exactly `docs/`, `LICENSES/`, `*.md`, `*.drawio`/`*.svg`/`*.png`. An Issue template, the root `LICENSE` and `*.rst` now count as relevant; submodule pins stay relevant.
- `scripts/measure_test_evidence.py` and its self-test: the budget pin includes `milan_dp`.
- Docs: `docs/testing/CI_WORKFLOWS.md`, `TESTING.md`, `RUNNING_TESTS.md`, the `milan_dp` and `milan_dp_gptp` READMEs, the `render_mutants.py` docstring, one `act_ci.py` comment.
Validation:
- `python3 scripts/suite_shards.py --selftest`: PASS. Planted `DEDICATED_SUITES = ()` gives 2 failures; hashing over `total` gives 6.
- `scripts/run_all_suites.sh --shard I/5 --list`, I = 0..4: 11/20/10/12/1 suites, union = the 54-suite serial inventory, each suite once, `milan_dp` only on 4/5. Workers 0-3 equal the old 0-3/4 minus `milan_dp`.
- `python3 scripts/ci_scope.py --selftest`: PASS
- `python3 scripts/ci_events.py --check`: OK, 1389 items. `--selftest`: PASS, 610 arms.
- `python3 scripts/act_ci.py --selftest`: PASS.
- Planted on copies, `ci_events.py --check --root <copy>`: an unmodified control exits 0. Each of these exits 1: the fifth worker removed (3 findings), the matrix and total back to 4 (2), the `4)` ownership arm removed (1), the ownership step removed (10), the docs-only line removed (1).
- Every workflow loads with `yaml.safe_load`; `bash -n scripts/run_all_suites.sh` and `py_compile` of every edited Python file pass.
- Whole `docs-check` list in workflow order, em-dash gate `--base f56fa168`, `measure_naming`/`measure_fail_fast`/`measure_test_evidence` last: 74 of 74 exit 0. Also green: `check_wire_accountability.py --self-test` and the `.git`-less `docs_check.py`/`check_feature_status.py`.
Acceptance criteria:
- The `milan_dp` hosted deadline: met by the measured 2700 s budget, above the worst case of about 1815 s. The two timeouts were the slow runner class, about 1 s and 13 s short of 1800 s. The first hosted run must confirm it.
- Own shard: met, shard 4/5.
- Nothing weakened: met; no suite, leg, check or count changed.
- Timeout stays red: met, exit 92 unchanged and pinned.
- Required aggregator waits for and judges every worker: met (`needs` the matrix, `--expect 5`, worker result required).
- Docs-only skip inside the workflow: already in place, now with the stated classification and a line in the gate.
- Force-push cancellation: verified, no change needed.
Open risks/questions:
- A decision is needed: on a docs-only diff the two exhaustive aggregates still report skipped, as the protected-merge-bar contract requires and the ruleset accepts; they do not run and report success, so the explanatory line is in the gate job.
- The classifier change applies to `rtl-fast`, `rtl-full` and `elaborate` alike.
- A hung `milan_dp` now costs up to 45 minutes of its own worker.
- Hosted evidence is pending the push. The first ready run must show five green Verilator workers, shard 4/5 running only `milan_dp` under 2700 s, and `verilator-suites` accepting `--expect 5` over 54 suites.

[A10] Merged: PR #480 into dev at c5bc3bfe (containment clean, review integrity clean, two independent POSITIVE reviews at 1b28b1ac after three rounds, hosted checks green on all three heads). Measured cause: nothing ran beside milan_dp; the slow hosted runner class already used 96 to 99 percent of the 1800 s budget, and the recent timeouts were killed 1 s and 13 s short of the end. milan_dp now runs alone on a fifth Verilator worker (19 min 32 s on its first hosted run; the required context green about 20 minutes after the workers start, was about 40) under a measured 2700 s budget; a timeout still exits 92 and fails the context. The review rounds also closed three holes that predate this change: the required aggregates' scripts were not pinned (an echo-only body passed the contract check), the pin normalization was not the shell's (a continuation, a no-break space or U+2028 passed and made the step exit 0 on a failed worker), and the docs-only classifier counted gate-read markdown as documentation and missed the source side of a rename. Remaining suggestions: https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/482.
